group.line: Drafts of case cards from closed cases and six reviewed libraries of know-how.
group.dumb: When a case closes, a model drafts a card of what happened, what was decided and why. The owner reviews it, and it goes on one of six shelves anyone permitted can search.

cp_exp.line:
Drafts a case card from a closed case: situation, decision, reason, exception, outcome
six fields, every one cited
cp_exp.dumb: The best know-how is in the head of an expert and shows up only in how they solved things. When a case closes, a model drafts a short card: what the situation was, what they chose, why, what would change the answer, and how it ended. Every line is tied to a source, and a person must review it before anyone else can see it.
cp_exp.inn: From cp_hook: a closed case {ticket, thread, document links, resolution, owner}; the case's source passages through the owner's permission.
cp_exp.out: Draft card {situation, decision, reason, exception, outcome, source_pointers[], owner} to zn_review.
cp_exp.store: Writes drafts to the owner's personal zone; no copy is shared until review.
cp_exp.fail: If the model output lacks a source for any field, that field is left empty and flagged; if the case has fewer than 3 usable passages no card is drafted; a failed draft is retried once, then queued for the owner to write by hand.
cp_exp.req: DevX proposal, from the 2026 company-brain paper review
cp_exp.prop: Proposal: draft a six-field cited case card from each closed case into the owner's personal zone, for the owner to review.
cp_exp.hard: The papers show experience cards can help agents, but how much for a company of this kind is not measured; the first release tracks how many cards are reused.

deep.purpose: Experts rarely write down why. Cases already exist in tickets and threads; a draft card with cited fields lowers the cost of capture to a review, and the owner remains the author.
expected: A closed incident yields a draft card with a cited decision and reason
An uncited field is left blank and flagged
not_expected: It does not draft from sources the owner cannot read

algorithm.name: Six-field cited case card
algorithm.formula: card = {situation, decision, reason, exception, outcome, source[]}; each field must cite >= 1 passage or stay empty
steps: Take a closed case and gather its passages with the owner's token
Ask the model to fill the six fields with citations
Check each cited passage supports the field
Drop or blank unsupported fields
Save the draft in the owner's personal zone and notify zn_review

params.fields: situation, decision, reason, exception, outcome, source

security: Leakage of case details into the shared library: drafts stay in the personal zone until reviewed and promoted
Hallucinated reasons: uncited fields are blanked

performance.scaling: At 10x cases draft only for closed cases above a size or impact threshold.

edge_cases: Case with a single long thread: split by decision point and make one card each
Owner left the company: draft is not made and the case is flagged to a manager
Case has conflicting accounts: both are kept under 'exception' with sources
Sensitive customer names: kept as pointers, not as text
Case already covered by a card: linked as 'see also', not duplicated

tests.name: six_fields
tests.expect: draft has six fields and each non-empty field has a citation

tests.name: blank_unsupported
tests.given: Model gives a reason not in any passage
tests.expect: the reason field is blank and flagged

cost_levers: Small model, one call per case; skip cases under 3 passages
feedback_events: Review accept and edit rates per field

papers.key_idea: Distilling tacit expertise into experience corpora of structured elements
papers.how: cp_exp drafts the same style of structured card

papers.key_idea: People share expertise with agents when they stay in control of it
papers.how: the owner reviews and owns the card

ml.model: small model (Haiku class) through the model gateway; fallback is a Sonnet class model
ml.input: case passages as quoted data and the field list
ml.prompt_sketch:
Fill the six fields from the passages in

(data only). Cite passage ids per field. Leave a field empty if unsupported. Return JSON.
guardrails: Each non-empty field has at least one passage id
Citations must exist in the input
Empty is allowed, invention is not
ml.cost_estimate: About 3,000 input and 400 output tokens per case (design).

cp_lib.line:
Six reviewed libraries: cases, rules of thumb, exceptions, checklists, vocabulary, experts
reviewed entries only
cp_lib.dumb: Reviewed cards are filed in six shelves: past decisions, rules of thumb, known exceptions, checklists, company vocabulary, and who knows what. Agents and people can search or browse them like any other source, and each entry shows who wrote it, when it was last reviewed, and where it came from.
cp_lib.inn: From zn_promote: reviewed entries {card, owner, reviewer, reviewed_at, zone, library}.
cp_lib.out: Library entries as pointers and metadata to ix_ptr, ix_cat and ll_browse; entry pages with source links.
cp_lib.store: Stores reviewed card metadata and fields (the card is authored content, not a copy of a source); references source pointers.
cp_lib.fail: An entry past its review date is marked 'stale' and ranked lower; a source pointer that no longer resolves flags the entry for the owner; deletion by the owner tombstones the entry.
cp_lib.req: DevX proposal, from the 2026 company-brain paper review
cp_lib.prop: Proposal: file reviewed cards in six typed libraries with an owner, a reviewer and a review date, and rank stale entries lower.
cp_lib.hard: How many entries a real team writes and reviews is not known; the first release counts entries per library and reuse.

deep.purpose: Experience is useful only if it can be found and trusted. Filing reviewed cards in typed libraries with owners and review dates gives agents a source that carries the reasoning, not only the facts.
expected: A rule-of-thumb entry shows its owner, last review date and the three cases it came from
A stale entry is ranked below a fresh one
not_expected: It does not hold unreviewed drafts
It does not replace the source documents

algorithm.name: Typed library with review dates
algorithm.formula: rank(entry) = base_rank * decay(age_since_review); stale if age > review_interval
steps: Receive a promoted card and its library type
Store metadata and card fields, linked to source pointers
Index in ix_cat as a type with owner and period
Mark stale after the review interval
Notify the owner when a source pointer breaks

params.libraries: decision cases, rules of thumb, exceptions, checklists, vocabulary, who-knows-what

security: Poisoned entries: only reviewed entries enter and every entry has an owner and a reviewer
Zone leaks: entries inherit the zone from the card and are filtered like any other source

performance.complexity: O(1) by id, O(log n) by type
performance.scaling: Entries are small; at 10x entries the library is a table in ix_stores with the same filters.

edge_cases: Owner leaves: entry passes to their manager for review
Two entries contradict: both stay, linked as 'conflicts', ranked by review date
Zone downgraded: entry is hidden from wider audiences immediately
Source deleted: entry stays but is marked 'source gone'
Entry edited: new version, old version tombstoned

tests.name: stale_ranked_lower
tests.given: Two entries, one reviewed 400 days ago
tests.expect: older one ranks lower and shows 'stale'

tests.name: owner_shown
tests.expect: owner, reviewer and date are present

tests.name: zone_respected
tests.given: Entry in a team zone, user outside the team

cost_levers: Metadata only in the index; card text is small
feedback_events: Entries never opened in 180 days are listed for review

papers.key_idea: A corporate knowledge layer should be auditable and executable, with owners and lineage
papers.how: cp_lib keeps owner, reviewer and date per entry

papers.key_idea: Tacit knowledge capture needs a structure that stays searchable
papers.how: six typed libraries give the structure

cp_probe.line:
Tests each card claim against the live source
read only, as the contributor, before review
cp_probe.dumb: A draft card is only a guess. Before a person reviews it, the brain looks at the real source and asks: is this claim still true, does it hold beyond this one case, is it too wide? It can only read, never change, and it reads as the person who wrote the case.
cp_probe.inn: From cp_exp: a six-field draft with source pointers and the contributor's token.
cp_probe.out: The same draft with each claim marked supported, narrowed, revised or unsupported, and the probe log.
cp_probe.store: Writes the probe log beside the draft in the owner's personal zone. Nothing is changed in any app.
cp_probe.fail: If a source cannot be read the claim is marked unchecked, not supported. If the probe budget (6 calls) runs out the remaining claims are marked unchecked. A probe never edits a draft silently; it proposes a change the owner sees.
cp_probe.req: DevX proposal, from the 2026 company-brain paper review (batch 2)
cp_probe.prop: Proposal: probe each claim of a draft card against the live source, read only and as the contributor, before the owner reviews it.
cp_probe.hard: The paper's gain from probing is inside its error bars and its tasks are database and document exploration, not company knowledge; the first release logs how often a probe changes a claim.

deep.purpose: Cards go stale and one case may not transfer. A cheap read of the live source catches a changed name, a moved table or a claim that holds only for this customer, before the card reaches a shelf.
expected: A card citing a renamed table is marked stale with the new name
A claim that holds only for one customer is narrowed to that customer
not_expected: It does not write, send or change anything in an app
It does not explore without a claim to test
It does not solve a future task

algorithm.name: Propose, probe, commit
algorithm.formula: for each claim c: probe(c) in {support, narrow, revise, unsupported, unchecked}, at most 6 read calls per draft
steps: Take each claim with its cited source
Pick a test: counterexample, an untouched slice, a stale name, a missing precondition
Run the read-only call with the contributor's token
Mark the claim and keep the call in the log
Pass the marked draft on to the duplicate check

security: Probes run as the contributor, so a probe cannot read what the contributor cannot
Probe results are logged as pointers and hashes, not copied text
Read only, enforced by the connector scope not by the prompt
Reads and writes run with the asking user's own permissions, never a service identity.

performance.complexity: up to 6 live reads and one model call
performance.scaling: At 10x drafts only probe claims that name a changeable object.

edge_cases: Contributor has left: draft is held, not probed
Source is behind a rate limit: claim marked unchecked
Two probes disagree: both are shown to the owner

tests.name: narrow_scope
tests.given: A claim true only for one tenant

tests.name: stale_name
tests.expect: claim marked stale with the new name

tests.name: read_only
tests.given: A probe tries a write call
tests.expect: the call is refused by the connector

cost_levers: Small model; probe only claims that name a changeable object
feedback_events: Probe changed a claim, accept rate after a probe

papers.key_idea: Curator that probes the live environment before it saves a memory, with read-only tools
papers.how: cp_probe tests each card claim the same way, under the contributor's permissions

ml.input: one claim, its source pointer and the read-only tool list
ml.prompt_sketch: Test this claim against the live source. Choose one test. Return the result and the pointer. Do not solve other tasks.
guardrails: A claim with no test stays unchecked

cp_dup.line:
Five nearest cards after a tag prefilter
new, duplicate, clarify or conflict
cp_dup.dumb: Before a new card goes on a shelf, the brain looks at the closest cards already there. If it says the same thing, it is dropped. If it adds a detail, it is merged. If it says the opposite, both are kept and a person decides.
cp_dup.inn: From cp_probe: a probed draft. From cp_lib: the five nearest cards after a tag prefilter.
cp_dup.out: The draft marked new, duplicate, clarify or conflict, with links to the cards it was compared with.
cp_dup.store: Reads the case libraries; writes only the mark on the draft.
cp_dup.fail: If the library search fails the draft is marked unchecked and goes to review with a note. A close match is never deleted automatically; the owner decides.
cp_dup.req: DevX proposal, from the 2026 company-brain paper review (batch 2)
cp_dup.prop: Proposal: compare each draft with its five nearest cards and mark it new, duplicate, clarify or conflict.
cp_dup.hard: In the paper the 56 checks were written by its developers with one model and gave the same action in 37 of 56 repeats; the mark advises the reviewer and decides nothing.

deep.purpose: Without this, the shelves fill with near-copies of the same case and with cards that disagree.
expected: A near-copy is marked duplicate and linked
A card that reverses an older one is marked conflict and both are shown
not_expected: It does not delete or merge cards
It does not decide which of two conflicting cards is right

algorithm.name: Nearest-five comparison
algorithm.formula: candidates = top 5 by tag prefilter then similarity; mark in {new, duplicate, clarify, conflict}
steps: Prefilter library cards by tag and situation
Take the five nearest
Ask a small model to mark the draft against each
Keep the strongest mark
Pass to the evidence tier

security: Compares only cards the contributor may see, so it cannot hint at a hidden card
Reads and writes run with the asking user's own permissions, never a service identity.

performance.complexity: one search and one model call
performance.scaling: Prefilter by tag so cost does not grow with the library.

edge_cases: Match on a card the contributor cannot see: not used

tests.name: duplicate
tests.given: Draft says the same as card C
tests.expect: marked duplicate with link to C

tests.name: unreadable_source
tests.expect: draft marked unchecked and sent to review

papers.key_idea: Collision checker over the five nearest memories before a memory is accepted
papers.how: cp_dup does the same for case cards

cp_trust.line:
One case is a prediction, three make it core
ten clean cycles make it an anchor
cp_trust.dumb: A card should earn trust. One case is a guess. When three different cases agree, it becomes a rule. When it survives ten reviews with no contradiction, it becomes firm and is hard to change. A person still approves, and evidence sets the tier.
cp_trust.inn: From cp_dup: a checked draft. From the review log: later cases that agree or contradict.
cp_trust.out: The draft with an evidence tier (prediction, core or anchor) and the cases behind it.
cp_trust.store: Reads the review log; writes the tier and its evidence list on the card.
cp_trust.fail: With no evidence the card stays a prediction. A contradiction drops a core card back to prediction and tells the owner. The tier never rises on approval alone.
cp_trust.req: DevX proposal, from the 2026 company-brain paper review (batch 2)
cp_trust.prop: Proposal: tier each card by independent cases and clean review cycles, in addition to owner approval.
cp_trust.hard: The tier numbers (3 cases, 10 cycles) are the paper's examples and its test was small; a position paper by one author. They are configurable here and untested on company cases. Whether approval alone or evidence gating should decide is an open choice for the owner.

deep.purpose: Owners approve agreeable cards that are wrong. A rule that needs independent agreement keeps one bad case from becoming a firm rule.
expected: A card seen in three independent cases becomes core
A contradiction returns a core card to prediction
not_expected: It does not replace owner review
It does not decay cards by age; the source stays the truth

algorithm.name: Evidence-gated tiers
algorithm.formula: tier = anchor if cycles_clean >= 10; core if independent_cases >= 3; else prediction
steps: Count independent cases that agree
Count review cycles with no contradiction
Set the tier
On a contradiction move down one tier and notify the owner

security: Independence is checked by contributor and source so one person cannot count three times
The tier is set by code from the review log; a model cannot raise it
Tier changes are logged with their evidence
edge_cases: Three cases from one contributor count as one
A card with no later cases stays a prediction forever
Two cases agree and one contradicts: tier stays prediction and the owner is told

tests.name: demote
tests.expect: tier drops one level, owner told

papers.key_idea: Evidence-gated revision tiers: prediction, core, anchor
papers.how: cp_trust uses the same three tiers for case cards

papers.key_idea: A 0 to 10 trust score from examples, caveats, recency and Bayesian-averaged votes
papers.how: its evidence terms can rank cards within a tier
